supersedes: The previous dark/neon/glassmorphism direction. Every rule below replaces it.

philosophy.one_line: Premium, editorial, tactile. The food is the interface; the numbers are the content.
reference_points: High-end food magazines and premium packaging
Anatomical plates and exploded technical drawings
philosophy.rhythm: Alternate impact and calm. Hero (calm) → burger anatomy (impact) → thesis (calm) → pizza builder (impact) → build your plate (calm) → feed. The loud sections only land because the quiet ones give the eye somewhere to rest.

forbidden: Gradients of any kind — backgrounds, text, borders, bars, 3D materials
Pill-shaped buttons, heavily rounded cards, card grids as a layout default
Stock fitness photography and generic AI illustration
Fabricated testimonials, statistics, logos or reviews

colour.rule: Solid colour only. Depth comes from value contrast, hairline rules and whitespace.

accent.usage: One accent, used sparingly: a heading's second line, an active state, a leader line, the plate control. Never a page background, never a large fill.

data_only.note: Food and macro colours belong to the food. They must never appear in page chrome.

colour.rules: Hairlines are cream at 10–12% alpha. Never pure black, never pure white.

typography.family: Archivo (400/500/700/800/900) for everything. One family, wide weight range.
typography.display: font-display, weight 800, tracking -0.035em, line-height 0.9. Fluid sizes: text-display-sm / -md / -lg.
typography.numbers: Numbers are content. Use .tnum (tabular figures) and the text-num-* scale, and animate value changes with useCountUp — never jump-cut a figure.
typography.labels: .label — 10px, 700, uppercase, 0.22em tracking, muted. Used for section numbers, units and captions.
typography.copy: Short. Prefer a line break over a comma. No paragraphs where a sentence will do.

surfaces_and_shape.radius: 2px. Effectively square. The only circle in the system is the Build Your Plate control.
surfaces_and_shape.panels: Solid .panel / .glass on a hairline border. No shadow.
surfaces_and_shape.borders: 1px. The previous 3px poster rules are gone — they read as brutalist, not editorial.

motion.principles: Short, eased, purposeful. Mechanical rather than bouncy. Nothing springs, nothing bounces, nothing pulses for attention.
motion.easing: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) for interface; easeOutExpo for counting numbers.
motion.scroll: Desktop uses pinned tall sections to scrub the food animations (useScrollProgress). Phones do not — the section collapses to normal flow and the animation plays on arrival (useInView). See BurgerAnatomy's `cinematic` flag.
motion.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion disables every animation and the pinned-scroll choreography, and defaults sound to off. Every scroll-driven state must also be reachable by a control.

food_experiences.count: Exactly two. Burger and pizza. Do not add a third — polish these instead.
food_experiences.burger: Deconstruction. Nine independently controllable layers, exploded on scroll, each clickable, with leader lines to labelled per-layer nutrition. Reassembles into the customised burger.
food_experiences.pizza: Construction. Base → sauce → cheese → toppings → bake → yours. The opposite gesture on purpose.
food_experiences.engine: src/food/FoodStack.jsx renders both. Layers are real separate objects, never a sliced-up flat image.
food_experiences.assets: src/food/manifest.js is the seam. Each layer names a transparent PNG; useLayerAssets probes the set at mount and falls back to geometry only if the whole set is missing. Photoreal artwork drops in at public/food/{burger,pizza}/ with no code change. Spec: 2048px wide, transparent, one ingredient per file, identical camera and lighting across a set, three-quarter view for the burger and top-down for the pizza.

data.rule: Nutrition comes from the API. Never hardcode a figure in the frontend and never ship a bundled shadow copy of the database.

endpoints./api/foods/components: Ingredient-level nutrition for the burger and pizza, priced per gram weight.
endpoints./api/foods/search: Dish-level search over the food database.
endpoints./api/weight, /api/progress/today, /api/p: History for the goal journey, daily progress and weekly rewind.

data.provenance: backend/food_components.py prefers data/food_database.csv wherever it carries the row, and falls back to IFCT 2017 / USDA FoodData Central constants only where it does not. Every component records which.
data.failure: If the API does not answer, say so and withhold the figures. Never display a plausible guess.

required: Semantic HTML; every control a real button with an accessible name
Visible focus rings in the accent colour — never removed
Colour is never the only carrier of meaning: the macro split bar also prints its percentages
Hit targets at least 36px, generous invisible hit slabs over small 3D geometry
Every scroll-driven state also reachable by a control

for_future_agents: Read this file before changing any visual code, and check a change against the `forbidden` list before shipping it.
When choosing between more features and better design, choose better design. Between more animation and better animation, better animation.
Do not reintroduce the feed's card grid as a layout pattern for new sections.
Keep the two food experiences at two.
